utterances.text: Now, explain this to me. Mr. Jasarevic is in Sarajevo. General Delic is in Sarajevo. Why are these bulletins being sent to Kakanj, to be delivered to General Delic, who is in Sarajevo most of the time?

utterances.speaker: ENVER BERBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the bulletins were sent, and I assume this, to Kakanj, if Mr. Jasarevic knew that he was somewhere outside Sarajevo, probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions. Mr. Menon?

utterances.speaker: MR. MENON
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just two questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, Witness, you were asked questions about information which pertained to prisoners of war. Would you agree with me that the reports from the corps dispatched daily information every day about large numbers of POWs?

utterances.speaker: ENVER BERBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not a frequent occurrence in the reports that I read.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But do you agree that it would be alarming, indeed, if it was written in the report that they were maltreated, not the fact in itself that they were captured? Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: ENVER BERBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with you. If I can amplify on that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: ENVER BERBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact that they were captured was actually a success, and that, per se, was not alarming.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But the fact that they were maltreated, that would be alarming?

utterances.speaker: ENVER BERBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be a special and specific situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just another question which stems from your own and Judge Lattanzi's question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 94 of Exhibit 377. I'm speaking about documents that were sent to you by Mr. Jasarevic or to Sacir Arnautovic. Take a look at this document. I asked you today to explain cryptographic protection, and the Prosecution showed you a series of documents of this kind which says "Sealed and signed." Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ENVER BERBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, tell us, is it not true that none of these documents is actually from Kakanj because it was not transmitted in this cryptographic-protected way, because it is not indicated in any of the document that this is the way in which it was sent, nor do they have a sign or -- a seal or signature? Do you agree that none of these documents came to Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: ENVER BERBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that any of these documents which were addressed to Colonel Sacir with this seal and signature did not come to Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So any document claimed to have come to Kakanj with a seal and signature could have been an original that could have been filed in Sarajevo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ENVER BERBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know that such a document was ever received in Kakanj because that stems from what you explained about cryptographic protection?

utterances.speaker: ENVER BERBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to consult the filing protocol to know whether they I had it right or not. I cannot tell on the basis of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. That concludes my questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That brings us to the conclusion of your testimony, sir. Thank you so much for coming to testify. You are excused and you may now stand down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that. Court adjourned to Monday morning at 9.00 in this court. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 17th day of September, 2007 at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.02 p.m.,
